subject: Blended term proposal & scaling path for NovaLabs renewal
messages:
From: Mark Goldstein <mark.gold@novalabs.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: 2026-11-02T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Planning for renewal — options for term & scale

Jonas / Marissa —

Our renewal for the platform is coming up Feb 1, 2027 and we want to lock in something that supports a predictable unit cost while giving us headroom for a material scale-up in Y2. Two asks up front:

1) Can we align the contract to our fiscal year (Jan 1 start) and co-term the various purchase orders?
2) We're considering a blended multi-year term (3 years) with a ramp schedule and annual true-ups. Need clarity on pricing for commit bands and what auto-renew looks like (opt-in vs opt-out).

I've attached a simple usage forecast and a matrix (nova_renewal_matrix_v2.xlsx) so you can see where the jumps are.

Also, procurement will want to see a term sheet and confirmation on invoice cadence — monthly vs quarterly — and any early-exit mechanics. Can you send a proposal that has: a conservative Year 1 commit, defined ramp steps for Year 2 & 3, and an auto-renew option that requires notice?

Thanks — happy to hop on a call next week.

—Mark
Mark Goldstein
Head of AI Platform, NovaLabs
mark.gold@novalabs.ai
From: jonas_weber@redwood.example
To: Mark Goldstein <mark.gold@novalabs.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example, priyom_das@redwood.example
Date: 2026-11-03T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Planning for renewal — options for term & scale

Hi Mark —

Thanks for the context and the forecast — helpful. We can definitely structure something to balance predictable unit economics with a growth path. Sketching a short proposal here and attaching a cleaner term draft (redwood_term_blend_draft_v1.pdf). High level:

• Start date & co-term: align to Jan 1, 2027 as requested; we'll co-term all line items to that boundary.
• Blended 3‑year option: Year 1 = 65% reserved commit of your current run-rate (lower entrance), Year 2 = +20% commit, Year 3 = +15% (final commit = 100%+ headroom).
• True-ups: annual true-up with a 30‑day reconciliation window. Overage rates tiered (discounted vs on-demand).
• Auto-renew: opt-in by default with a 60‑day notice to opt-out; can switch to opt-out model if procurement needs that language (we can add an explicit notice period).
• Billing cadence: quarterly invoicing by default; can shift to monthly if you prefer (note slight price delta if monthly).

Next steps if this aligns: 1) review attached draft and the renewal matrix; 2) we set a 30‑min call with procurement to confirm PO/DocuSign flow and SOC2 evidence; 3) we'll prepare a redlined term sheet for signature.

Can you confirm availability for a call on Tue (11/9) or Wed (11/10)?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Mark —

Looping in a few implementation notes from our side:

• Onboarding milestones: if you accept the blended commit we can frontload a set of onboarding credits to cover the first month of heavier ingestion/embedding conversions — helps avoid early overage charges.
• Technical ramp plan: Priyom, our SE, will coordinate a phased rollout: pilot (30 days), expand (month 2–6), steady-state (month 7+). We can align milestones to payment tranches if that helps NovaLabs' cashflow.
• Reporting: we'll provide token-level cost dashboards and a monthly usage forecast feed so you can see when true-ups might hit.

Attaching the draft term sheet Jonas shared; pricing bands are in the matrix. Happy to take procurement-specific asks on the call.

Best,

Marissa / Jonas —

Thanks for the outline. A couple of procurement items we need clarified before the call:

1) Can you confirm whether the blended term requires any minimum annual spend (we'd like the flexibility to true-up without penalties if actual usage undershoots the commit in Y1).
2) SOC 2 and data locality: where will Tier 1 logs and audit trails be retained? We need the SOC 2 report and a statement on audit log retention for at least 12 months.
3) DocuSign vs PO: our standard process is PO + vendor signature; we'll need a simple signature flow that creates an invoiceable PO line.

Finally, please add details in the term sheet about early-exit (pro-rated refund or credit model) — we've seen ambiguous language in other vendors' contracts.

Elena Park
Senior Procurement Manager, NovaLabs
elena@novalabs.ai
From: jonas_weber@redwood.example
To: Elena Park <elena@novalabs.ai>, Mark Goldstein <mark.gold@novalabs.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example, priyom_das@redwood.example
Date: 2026-11-10T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Planning for renewal — options for term & scale

Elena / Mark —

Thanks — answers inline and next steps below. (Quoted your note for context.)

> 1) Min annual spend and penalties
We propose Year 1 have a floor equal to 50% of your current committed run-rate (no penalties if usage is below floor; instead we provide an annual reconciliation and carry-forward credit that can be used against Y2). The goal here is flexibility in Y1 to smooth adoption risk.

> 2) SOC 2 & audit logs
We'll provide the latest SOC 2 Type II report via a secure ShareFile link during the procurement call; audit logs (token-level access logs and infra traces) retained for 12 months by default, with optional extended retention as an add-on. I'll include the SOC2 link in the DocuSign package.

> 3) DocuSign vs PO
We can accept a PO and apply a vendor-signed agreement; for speed we typically issue a DocuSign term sheet that NovaLabs then supplies a PO against. We'll note both flows in the term sheet and mark invoice cadence as quarterly by default (monthly on request).

> Early-exit language
We'll add a pro‑rated credit model in Year 1 and a clear schedule of refunds/credits for any early termination in the draft.

Attached are the updated term draft and the renewal matrix (redwood_term_blend_draft_v1.pdf; nova_renewal_matrix_v2.xlsx). If this aligns, proposed call time: Wed 11/17 at 10am PT — 30 minutes to confirm procurement flow and finalize DocuSign. After call we'll post the redlined term sheet to HubSpot (HS-234768) and route to your procurements queue.

Next steps:
• Confirm 11/17 10am PT or suggest another slot.
• If you want monthly invoices instead of quarterly, let us know and we'll mark pricing accordingly.

Appreciate it — looking forward to closing this so you can scale.

Jonas Weber
Sr. Account Executive — Redwood Inference
